analysis:
The changes are documentation only.

- **docs/operations/desktop-release.md:** the base said there was no update feed (base lines 66-68). The head embeds a fixed generic electron-updater feed at the `desktop-latest` release (head lines 72-88). Assets are replaced on each tag, with `latest-mac.yml` uploaded last. The app checks at launch and every 4 hours and installs on quit. The head claims macOS signature-match enforcement (line 84), and the workflow verifies sha512 and size (lines 64-66). Rollback means re-uploading the prior `latest-mac.yml`, since there are no downgrades (lines 103-106).
- **docs/developer/desktop-app.md (head lines 554-556):** replaces the 'choose and host the feed' step with a verification step. The release-qualification and CLI-install text (lines 540-639) is unchanged apart from that step.

The new fleet-wide GUI update channel creates new attack surface that the threat model does not cover; this is recorded as a low finding. The GUI drives the provider CLI, which holds A-008 tokens; the CLI path and its signature check (`Backend.verifyRuntime`, line 638) are unchanged.

No evidence was supplied for:
- `.github/workflows/release-desktop.yml`
- `desktop-app/scripts/update-feed.mjs`
- `desktop-app/src/main/updates.ts` and `updateFeed.ts`

Integration should verify three things: the updater rejects non-https or non-generic feeds, Squirrel's designated-requirement check is not weakened, and workflow token permissions on `desktop-latest` are limited. No provider runtime, attestation, cache (T-041) or coordinator behavior changed.

findings.detail:
The PR documents that each desktop release now auto-updates every installed app from a mutable GitHub release, `desktop-latest`, whose assets are replaced on each tag (head lines 72-88, 9-10). The GUI installs, repairs and drives the provider CLI. The canonical model covers signed provider artifacts (T-013, T-034, A-011, A-017) and the operator boundary (TB-003). It does not describe this channel.

Authenticity rests on Squirrel.Mac checking the Developer ID designated requirement (line 84). The `latest-mac.yml` sha512 values come from the same mutable release, so they give integrity only, not authenticity. A compromised releaser, repository token or workflow could therefore push any app signed by team SLDQ2GJ6TL to the whole fleet without user action. That app is installed on quit.

Rollback relies on a higher version, because the updater never downgrades (lines 103-106). The release workflow and updater code are not supplied, so the feed checks and pinned designated requirement are unverified.

Fix: add a trust boundary and threat for the desktop update feed. It should state that signature verification is the sole authenticity control, cover protection of `desktop-latest` and workflow permissions, and restate the no-downgrade and rollback limits. Also confirm the updater pins the team and bundle-ID requirement.
findings.title: New GUI auto-update channel on every provider Mac is not in the threat model
